display.title: The Great Favor
display.summary_short: The power of simcha and of doing a favor for another Jew: the Rebbe's reply to a man who stopped him on the street, and the poor tailor whose brachos came true.
display.summary_long: After the song "I Believe in Hashem", the storyteller explains the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to serve Hashem with joy: the Zohar says that blessings are given according to the face we show, and the Rebbe explained that the Alter Rebbe answered his interrogators' last question with a smile. Then come two stories about the power of a favor. A man from Boro Park stops the Rebbe on the street for advice; when a yeshivah student scolds him, he writes an apology, and the Rebbe replies that a neshamah may come into the world for decades just to do one favor for another Jew. In the second story, two students of the Baal Shem Tov meet Yankel, a sad, silent tailor in Vilna whose blessings always come true, as a wealthy flax dealer revealed one day when he had drunk too much. At the Baal Shem Tov's request Yankel comes to Mezhibuzh and tells his life story: years earlier he gave away every ruble he had earned to free a Jewish family from a poritz's dungeon. The Baal Shem Tov tells him that this is why his blessings come true, and takes him in as a student.
display.lesson: Serve Hashem with simcha, and do favors for other Jews, especially when it is hard; that may be the very purpose of our neshamah in this world.

advisories.note: A poritz keeps a Jewish family in his dungeon for unpaid rent until they are ransomed.
A dangerous poritz when drunk; a merchant gets drunk at a party and tells his secret.
A poor tailor falls into sadness and has to beg.
